[web - flash] Battalion Nemesis - what's the next best thing to Advance Wars? A clone of Advance Wars.

The Battalion series has several entries, this is the first and there were some improvements from game to game so if you just want to get an impression of the end result then check out the final game in the series, Battalion: Vengeance.

This is quite clearly a clone of Advance Wars, but that's not a bad thing. For anyone unaware Advance Wars was originally a first party Game Boy Advance game, and it's ostensibly a turn-based strategy game... but it isn't really. The way it plays is much closer to a combat-themed puzzle game. You're presented with a scenario where you and the enemy both have units in play and you need to find a way to make that situation work for you. It's much less about employing a strategy than it is about find the right combination of moves to solve the puzzle.

My mom usually made breakfast when I was young. Sometimes my dad would give it a shot, and it was usually something easy. His go to choice was hot cereal like Malt O Meal or Cream of Wheat. It always came out lumpy, and even though this wasn't his intention, the lumps were like awesome little dumplings. I still can't figure out how he did it. I love my dad.
Dad made the best hot cereal
The lumps came from not stirring the cereal thoroughly while it was cooking. Your dad was doing it correctly as far as I am concerned - I am firmly in the "lumps are awesome" camp.

I had the same experience growing up. I also asked my dad to make it lumpy.

Anyway, if you want to specifically cook it so it does have lumps, the trick is to pour the whole pre-measured amount into the boiling water at once, rather than slowly whisking it in. Ideally, to make a smooth, no-lump product, you would slowly whisk in the mix into lukewarm water and then add heat while continuously whisking until fully cooked.
